question.text: Not to be accused of lacking attention to detail, Amin also clarified that he was the conqueror of this country "in Particular". Idi Amin brutally ruled this country for most of the 1970s, during which he expelled all Asians from it.
question.clue: A 2012 documentary was released by Invisible Children to combat this country's Lord's Resistance Army, led by Joseph Kony.

swap.leadin: Name these dictators who are still alive.
swap.text: This Libyan outlined his philosophies in the Green Book. He also released the Lockerbie bomber and, in a United Nations speech, suggested partitioning Switzerland.
swap.clue: This leader advocated for direct democracy through the system of Jamahiriya.

question.leadin: Stories of this ruler's largesse include a legend that he built a mosque every Friday during one of his travels.
question.text: Name this 14th century Mansa of the Mali Empire, best known for a legendary hajj.
question.clue: The architect Abu Isaq al Saheli was commissioned by this ruler to build the Djinguereber mosque.

swap.leadin: This country's late 1960s civil war began with the secession of a state populated by its Igbo [ig-BOW] people.
swap.text: Name this African country, which fought a civil war against the state of Biafra. This country's capital was moved to Abuja in 1991.
swap.answerHtml: Nigeria [or Federal Republic of Nigeria; accept Nigerian Civil War]
swap.clue: Newswatch founder Dele Giwa was killed by a bomb supposedly ordered by this country's president Ibrahim Babangida.

question.text: The burning of the USS Philadelphia occurred after it was captured in the harbor of this city. The First Barbary War began after Yusuf Karamanli, the pasha of this city, declared war on the US.
question.clue: The USS Intrepid was downed during a blockade of this city's harbor, and this city's ruling family was defeated at the Battle of Derna; those events are cited in the second line of the US Marines' Hymn which refers to this city's shores.

swap.leadin: Dag Hammarskjold died in a plane crash en route to negotiations with this region's leader.
swap.text: Name this region of the Congo that became a breakaway state under Moise Tshombe in 1960.
swap.clue: This region was joined in an independence movement by South Kasai, and its largest city is Lubumbashi.

question.text: Rhodes was Prime Minister of the Cape Colony, a settlement in this modern-day country. In this modern-day country, Afrikaans-speaking Boers fought two wars against the British Empire.
question.clue: In that song, musicians pledged to not play at a casino resort in this country, "Sun City".

swap.text: This Berber man criticized the nudity of the mansa's female servants in his account of Mali. He recorded decades of travel after his dream of an eagle inspired his extended hajj.
swap.answerHtml: ibn Battuta [or Abu Abdullah Muhammad Ibn Battuta; or Shams ad-Din]
swap.clue: He befriended Bayalun, the daughter of the Byzantine emperor Andronicus who had been married to Khan Ozbeg of the Golden Horde, and accompanied her to Constantinople.

question.text: "Pulling together" or "Harambee" is the slogan used to unite this country since its 1963 independence. For fifteen points, name this nation on the equator bounded by Tanzania, Uganda, Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia.
question.clue: The kipande system forced natives in this country to work and the Kapurenga 6 were a group of nationalists in this country.

swap.leadin: An army led by Paul Kagame helped end this conflict, whose resolution was done in part by local gacaca courts.
swap.text: Name this 1994 atrocity in which radio messages about "cockroaches" and "tall trees" inspired Hutus to kill their Tutsi neighbors.
swap.clue: Widespread rape during this event led to a huge spike in HIV infections.

question.leadin: Name these following about a race described in Greek myth.
question.text: Supposed to live in Scythia or northern Asia Minor, this race of female warriors cut off their right breasts in order to better utilize a bow and arrow.
question.clue: Athens was attacked by them in the Attic War, an attempt to rescue their queen Hippolyta.

swap.text: The Herero people are members of this larger ethnic group. These people brought agriculture to Sub-Saharan Africa upon their migration in the first century BCE, and name a language family that includes Swahili.
swap.clue: This people who settled throughout the lower savannahs and would eventually split into numerous tribes including the Zulu and Sukuma.

question.text: Among the groups battled against by Askia Muhammad during his reign was this loose confederation of states, named for the dominant people of northern Nigeria and southwestern Niger, which was positioned between the Songhai and Kanem-Bornu empires.

swap.leadin: In the early 18th century, this empire recruited scouts to clear brush, blaze false trails, and drain standing water based on medical expertise that included a precursor of germ theory.
swap.text: Name this empire whose founder Osei Tutu ("OH-say TOO-too") modernized its army with tactics he learned from the Akwamuhene ("ah-KWAH-moo-hay-nay"). Many houses had indoor plumbing in this empire's city of Kumasi.
swap.clue: This state's unifier founded his capital on the site where a Kum tree planted by the priest Okomfo Anokyo prospered; that king, who also defeated the Denkyira, was Osei Tutu.

question.text: This queen from the Zenata succeeded Kusaila as leader of the Berber resistance. Although her victory at the 698 Battle of Meskiana was absolute, whether she was pagan, Christian, or Jewish remains uncertain to this day.
question.clue: This mysterious "Queen of the Berbers" led revolts in North Africa against the Umayyads in the 7th century AD, and was given a name meaning "witch," possibly for being Jewish. According to Ibn Khaldun, she caused no end of trouble for the general Hasan ibn al-Nu'man, but was eventually killed by him.

swap.text: This man served as the first democratically elected president of the Republic of Congo for ten weeks until he was deposed and assassinated.
swap.clue: Soon after concluding independence talks with King Baudouin ("bow-DWAHN"), this leader was forced to take refuge in Stanleyville when he was dismissed by Joseph Kasa-Vubu.

question.leadin: Brutal "eye for an eye" reprisals during this war were carried out by commanders such as Fernando Robles.
question.text: Name this war, part of a larger colonial conflict, that resulted in Agostinho Neto ("ah-goosh-TEEN-yoo NET-oo") taking power. This war was ended by the Alvor Agreement.
question.answerHtml: Angolan War of Independence [prompt on Portuguese Overseas War; prompt on Portuguese Colonial War; prompt on Guerra do Ultramar]

swap.text: The Desert Column sent to relieve the Siege of Khartoum was intercepted by Mahdist forces at this battle near some wells. Tory parliamentary candidate and British national hero Frederick Burnaby was speared in the throat in this battle.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Abu Klea [accept Battle of Abu Tͅuleiħ ]

question.leadin: Name these empires or dynasties that ruled Ethiopia, FTPE.
question.text: Early in the 4th century A.D., it became a Christian empire under King Ezana. Ge'ez was the language of this empire, which conquered Meroe and was a trading powerhouse until it had faded away by 900 AD.

swap.text: This Congregationalist minister switched from allying with Nkomo to Mugabe to accusing Mugabe of trying to assassinate him before Mugabe had him arrested. He recalled his role in ending white rule in African Nationalism and Roots of a Revolution and also wrote a novel, The Polygamist.
swap.clue: This founder of the ZANU was a former Congregationalist minister and president of the African Teachers Association, who wrote such works as African Nationalism and the novel The Polygamist before falling out with Mugabe in the 80s.
